accepted.question_text: Let m be a fixed positive integer and let F_m = {j in 2Z \ {0} : |j| <= m}. For a vector z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) in C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = sum_{x in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x), where X_n^+(F_m) is the set of all admissible walks from -n to n whose steps are positive elements of F_m, a walk x has intermediate vertices j(t) that never equal +n or -n before the endpoint, and h(x) = h_1(x) prod_t V(x(t)) with h_1(x) = prod_t (n^2 - j(t)^2)^(-1). Determine the polynomials P_{m,n}(z), or at least determine their asymptotic behavior when m is fixed and n tends to infinity.

accepted.question_text: Let F_m be a finite set of permitted steps and define β_n^+ = sum_{x in X_n(F_m)} h(x), where X_n(F_m) is the set of admissible walks from -n to n with steps in F_m and h(x) is the walk weight used earlier in the paper. Proposition 4 states that β_n^+ = (sum_{x in X_n^+} h(x)) [1 + O(log n / n)] provided the inequality sum_{x in X_n^+} |h(x)| <= C(V) |sum_{x in X_n^+} h(x)| holds. Is this inequality true for almost every parameter vector z = {V} in C^m, and what is the structure of the exceptional set W = { z : C(z) = infinity } for which such a bound fails?
